direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is very much a surrealist Wes Anderson-esque style set in the reconstruction era, though a little all over the place (especially by the end); the direction on a microscale is not the best because you do not really care about these characters, so their interpersonal scenes feel like a chore to get through; the storytelling is fine in some moments as you can see the clear conflict of the disease and how it is affecting the town, but it comes completely out of left field in the last 30-40 minutes; the storytelling also just feels very boring for the most part because it feels like they are trying to stretch out the plot; the tension is non-existent because the movie feels like such a chore to get through with how slow it is, so you don't really care about any of these characters because of how boring it can get at times

performance.comments: Kind of plays a pretty deadpan character that you don't really care for, especially with the material he is given
Feels very much like wasted talent for this movie because they give him such a boring character with not the best material to work with

Plays the struggle for the character decently well as you care for her struggle to try and save her baby, but the material she has to work with doesn't present the best dynamic between her and Flynn (though she makes the most of what she can)

cast.comments: The cast is filled with so many minor characters that come and go throughout the movie, not really making an imprint

story.comments: The concept is somewhat interesting to see a reconstruction town and the effects of a disease spreading throughout the town and how it affects people, but the movie tries to stretch out its very little plot in such a surrealist way that it feels both left field and boring; the plot structure is a major issue for this movie because they try to stretch out such a small plot, and the climax is poorly executed as it is this surrealist dream sequence that ultimately makes the whole movie just feel pretty boring; character writing is not great because while they are written with struggles and trauma, you don't really care for any of them

screenplay.comments: The dialogue, while accurate to the time period, is honestly pretty boring as many scenes are just two-person conversations to fill time; the symbolism is for sure there, I was just too bored to even care or decode it; the foreshadowing is there too, but I was too checked out to read that deep into this movie

score.comments: Very minimal score, making the movie feel pretty slow at points; when the score is used, it's mainly for setting tone and tension

cinematography.comments: Shot well in the Academy aspect ratio as it is the key highlight for the movie; the cinematography feels very Wes Anderson-esque with its fast pivots and pans, helping mitigate the issues with its slow pacing; the camera really is another character in the movie and helps keep you somewhat interested, until it's too late

editing.comments: Works well in conjunction with the cinematography to make this feel like a surrealist Wes Anderson movie with its fast cuts between its camera angles and the zooms on subjects

visual_effects.comments: Makes the movie feel pretty surrealist

production_design.comments: Transports you to a reconstruction era Wisconsin, and does a pretty good job helping the aesthetic for the movie; the surrealist sets were well designed as well

makeup.comments: Sells the disease, dirt, and grime of being sick during this time period

costumes.comments: Time period accurate to transport you back to 1870s America

review.pacing: Pacing is unbearably slow for this movie as there is barely any plot they try to go through, making the movie feel boring and like a chore to get through (a good 15-20 minutes could have been cut to make it somewhat more entertaining)
review.climax: Climax is just so uninteresting with how out of left field they take the story to where you are counting down to when the movie will finally end, even edging you the final 5 minutes before the credits roll
review.tone: Tone is very much a surrealist Wes Anderson-esque movie set during the reconstruction era
review.overall: Overall, 'A Prayer for the Dying' plays like a surrealist Wes Anderson-esque period drama that is stylistically pleasing with its cinematography and sets, but is ultimately such a chore to get through as the film stretches such a small plot with characters you don't really care about, making it feel so boring that by the end you are just hoping the credits come soon (especially with how out of left field they take the climax)
